whatChanged: ADVANCED: Nvidia's OpenAI data-center backstop is now firm and sized -- up to $105bn of credit for the first 4.25GW of the SB Energy-built PORTS-Pike campus in Pike County, Ohio, with an option covering a further 3.75GW (nvda-openai-datacenter-backstop) (rumored → confirmed)
NEW: Nvidia invests $1.5bn in SoftBank's SB Energy and takes sole-supplier status for compute at the Ohio campus it is also financing, with access to up to 8GW of capacity (nvda-sbenergy-investment)

NEW: TTM Technologies agrees to buy defence electronics maker Epiq Solutions for $1.1bn in cash, funded entirely with new term loans and taking net leverage to ~2.3x at closing (ttmi-epiq-acquisition)
NEW: Alibaba agrees to sell its entire stake in game developer Lingxi Games to Trustar Capital for more than $2bn, roughly double June's indicative value (baba-lingxi-games-divestiture)

themes.label: Public-to-private buyout offers on listed companies
themes.note: Sponsor-, sovereign- and strategic-led buyouts keep pulling listed names off public markets, and the top end of the pipeline is still filling: Silver Lake is in talks to take Workday private at a ~$43bn market value (wday-silverlake-takeover-talks) and Thoma Bravo has signed a $4bn+ take-private of Accelerant barely a year after its NYSE listing (arx-thoma-bravo-take-private). Already signed: Bernhard Capital's $43-a-share deal for engineering consultancy Bowman (bwmn-bernhard-capital-takeover), Blackstone Infrastructure's Safe Harbor buying MarineMax at $53 a share (hzo-safe-harbor-acquisition), Nielsen's $13.60-a-share deal for DoubleVerify (dv-nielsen-acquisition), Apollo's firm 715p easyJet offer (ezj-apollo-takeover), KKR's $127-a-share agreement for Integer Holdings (itgr-kkr-takeover) and the completed $55bn PIF-Silver Lake-Affinity buyout of EA (ea-pif-consortium-take-private). Still unresolved: CVC and Veritas Capital are running competing GBP1.56bn proposals for Bodycote to a 2 September deadline (boy-cvc-takeover-bid, boy-veritas-takeover-bid), Grant Thornton and New Mountain Capital's $5bn deal for CBIZ runs a go-shop to August 27 (cbz-grant-thornton-acquisition), Pacific Equity Partners' SG Fleet vehicle bids A$3.60 a share for FleetPartners (fpr-sgfleet-takeover-bid), Trian is assembling co-investors behind a take-private of Wendy's (wen-trian-takeover-bid), InMode's special committee is free to act again now that the Haifa court has thrown out Steel Partners' injunction request (inmd-steel-partners-buyout), Curaleaf has gone straight to Aurora Cannabis shareholders with a US$4.00-a-share hostile bid (acb-curaleaf-takeover-bid), and ADW Capital's $18-a-share proposal for Driven Brands was dismissed as lacking a credible basis (drvn-adw-capital-takeover-bid).

themes.label: UK-listed franchises broken up or taken private
themes.note: The London market keeps losing control of its own constituents to overseas and private capital, from the FTSE 100 down into the FTSE 250's industrials. Bodycote, the largest independent thermal-processing network in the West, has twin cash approaches a penny apart -- CVC at up to 915p (boy-cvc-takeover-bid) and Veritas Capital at up to 914p (boy-veritas-takeover-bid) -- with the board running both through confirmatory due diligence ahead of the 2 September Rule 2.6 deadline. Above them, Apollo's 715p-a-share, GBP5.7bn cash offer for easyJet is firm and board-recommended after Castlelake walked away (ezj-apollo-takeover), and Prologis has a recommended Rule 2.7 offer valuing Segro at ~GBP14.3bn that would remove one of the FTSE 100's largest REITs from the LSE (pld-sgro-takeover-bid).

themes.label: AI data-center capacity and power build-out
themes.note: Capital keeps pouring into the physical layer of AI compute, and the constraint has narrowed to energised power rather than plans for it. The Ohio megaproject is now the clearest example: Nvidia's backstop for OpenAI's PORTS-Pike campus has firmed up at up to $105bn of credit for the first 4.25GW, with an option covering a further 3.75GW (nvda-openai-datacenter-backstop), and Nvidia has separately put $1.5bn of equity into developer SB Energy, which with SoftBank plans at least 10GW of new generation, a 9.2GW on-site gas plant costing ~$33bn and $4.2bn of Ohio grid investment (nvda-sbenergy-investment). Elsewhere Core Scientific paid ~$444m to take ~440MW of in-service, grid-connected Oklahoma capacity off a rival miner and push its Muskogee campus toward 1.5GW of AI colocation (corz-polaris-acquisition), while Williams is paying up to $5.5bn for Momentum Midstream to connect Haynesville gas to Gulf Coast LNG and power demand (wmb-momentum-midstream-acquisition). How the build gets funded is the other half of the story: Nvidia has signed MOUs with six of the largest private-capital pools to mobilise over $500bn of third-party financing (nvda-compute-financing-platforms), Intel is selling $15bn of new stock to fund fab capex (intc-equity-offering-2026) and Amazon's 2026 capex guide is up to ~$220bn with capacity constrained into 2027 (amzn-capex-raise-2026). On the equipment side Prysmian pays ~$3.8bn for Atkore's conduit and cable-management business (atkr-prysmian-acquisition) and Everus bought modular electrical specialist Epsilon Industries (ecg-epsilon-acquisition); at the silicon layer Sony and TSMC are putting JPY747bn into a Kumamoto image-sensor fab (sony-tsmc-image-sensor-jv), Doosan took control of Korea's sole wafer maker SK Siltron (doosan-sksiltron-acquisition), and Nvidia will co-design orbital compute payloads with SpaceX (spcx-nvda-starmind-partnership).

themes.label: Signed M&A deals hitting regulatory or legal roadblocks
themes.note: Deals investors thought were settled keep being decided by courts and state regulators rather than at closing -- and this week the pattern sharpened into a pure courtroom problem. Paramount Skydance has now satisfied every regulatory condition in its Warner Bros. Discovery merger agreement, with Mexico's August 14 clearance completing 68 jurisdictions, yet it still cannot close until five days after a 12-day antitrust trial set for March 2, 2027, owing Warner holders ~$7m a day from September 30, 2026 in the meantime (psky-wbd-acquisition). Delaware's Chancery Court has voided Verisk's walk-away from its $2.35bn AccuLynx purchase, ordering it to try again while the FTC review that triggered the termination is still unfinished (vrsk-acculynx-acquisition). Western Union's Intermex deal cleared New York's DFS on August 14 only for California's DFPI to suspend its own approval extension the day before (imxi-westernunion-acquisition). The one roadblock that has come down is InMode's: the Haifa court denied Steel Partners' injunction request in its entirety, releasing the special committee to rule on the competing buyout bids (inmd-steel-partners-buyout).

themes.label: Chipmakers funding or locking in the customers that buy their chips
themes.note: Vendor financing and exclusivity remain the standard shape of frontier-AI deals, and this week Nvidia extended the model from credit into ownership. Its OpenAI backstop is now a firm commitment of up to $105bn against the first 4.25GW of the Ohio campus rather than an open-ended guarantee over the whole 10GW project (nvda-openai-datacenter-backstop), and alongside it Nvidia has taken a $1.5bn equity stake in campus developer SB Energy that makes it the sole supplier of compute on the site it is financing (nvda-sbenergy-investment) -- the circularity critics object to, written into the cap table. The syndicated version keeps scaling too: the six-firm compute-financing platforms are designed to lend against Nvidia's own GPUs so labs, enterprises and clouds can afford to buy them, moving the credit risk to Apollo, BlackRock, Blackstone, Brookfield, Goldman Sachs and KKR rather than carrying it in-house (nvda-compute-financing-platforms). The pure lock-in version continues alongside: SpaceX has committed exclusively to building its AI infrastructure on NVIDIA platforms, with the two co-designing orbital compute payloads (spcx-nvda-starmind-partnership).
